 State Representative Patrick Sellers is expected to turn himself in to federal authorities Thursday morning on fraud charges. 
 Follow Unfollow Recent posts By Josh Moon Follow Unfollow Recent posts Josh Moon is an investigative reporter and columnist. Published November 19, 2026 Read online: https://www.alreporter.com/2026/11/19/sources-state-rep-sellers-indicted-on-fraud-charges
 Listen Share Share article
 Bluesky X Facebook LinkedIn Email Copy link Print Save Comments Questions Listen Save Comments Share State Representative Patrick Sellers in an official portrait. Advertisement
 State Representative Patrick Sellers is expected to turn himself in Thursday morning on federal fraud charges, sources told APR late Wednesday night. 
 Specifics regarding the charges against the Birmingham-area representative were not disclosed by the two sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren’t authorized to disclose the information publicly.

 Copy instruction Open ChatGPT (opens in a new tab) The U.S. Attorney’s office for the Northern District of Alabama issued a media advisory on Wednesday evening announcing plans for an 11 a.m. press conference. The alert stated that U.S. Attorney Phil Williams and FBI ASAC Grady Fisher will be “announcing the unsealing of charges in a case involving allegations of fraud by a public official.” The alert provided no indication of the specifics of the charges or who might be the target. 
 Sellers, who is a pastor, took office as the District 57 state representative in 2022. He was re-elected without opposition to his seat just two weeks ago.
